c.tagline: Korea's volcanic holiday island — Hallasan's peak, lava-rock coasts, and endless beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Hail on the street or book via Kakao T; all taxis are metered. On Jeju, taxis handle airport runs and short hops, but most visitors rent a car to tour the island's coast and Hallasan trailheads.

hood_desc: Jeju City's historic downtown, built around the Dongmun Traditional Market, the Chilseong-ro shopping arcade and the old Gwandeokjeong pavilion. A walkable, atmospheric base for street food, markets and local life close to the harbor.

The 'new city' district of Yeon-dong, Jeju's hub for hotels, department stores, duty-free shopping and the neon Nuwemaru pedestrian street where the island's dining and nightlife concentrate. Best for travelers who want modern comforts and things open late.

A newer residential quarter near the Halla Arboretum and several of Jeju's larger resort hotels — quieter and greener than downtown but still minutes from the airport and Sinjeju. Suits families and travelers with a rental car.

Jeju City's northern seafront, running from Tapdong Plaza along the coast to the lava-formed Yongduam (Dragon Head Rock) and the Yongyeon gorge. Great for sunset walks, cafes and easy sightseeing by the water.
A relaxed beach neighborhood west of the center, known for Iho Tewoo Beach with its horse-shaped lighthouses and shallow swimming water. A calm, local-feeling spot for a seaside stay.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though most locals prefer bottled or filtered.

transit.pay: Tap a T-money or Cashbee card on boarding and again on transfer; a single ride is about ₩1,150-1,200 with free transfers within 40 minutes. Cash is accepted but exact change is expected. There is no rail or metro anywhere on Jeju.
transit.hours: City and intercity buses run roughly 6:00 AM to around 10:00 PM (a few airport-linked routes later); after that, taxis and Kakao T fill the gap. Many visitors rent a car to reach the coast and Hallasan trailheads.

ferry: Jeju Port (car ferries to Wando, Mokpo and mainland Korea)

transit.m: Airport Limousine Bus (600) to Jeju City and Seogwipo hotels
Taxi to Jeju City center, 10-15 min

tip.r: Not customary in Korea; tipping is not expected.

food.name: Heuk-dwaeji black pork
food.desc: Jeju's native black pigs give firm, deeply flavoured belly and neck cuts, grilled at the table and dipped in anchovy sauce.

places.name: Black Pork Street
places.note: A short strip lined on both sides with black-pork barbecue houses.

places.name: Donsadon
places.note: The place that made Jeju black pork famous with visitors; expect a queue.

places.name: Suksungdo
places.note: Specialises in dry-aged belly and less common cuts of the black pig.

food.name: Haemul ttukbaegi
food.desc: A bubbling earthenware pot of the day's catch: abalone, octopus, prawns and shellfish in a clean, briny broth.

places.name: Dongmun Traditional Market
places.note: Market kitchens cook the seafood you can see on the stalls outside.

places.name: Yongduam coast restaurants
places.note: Row of seafood houses along the rock coast, best at sunset.

food.name: Jeonbokjuk abalone porridge
food.desc: Silky rice porridge stained green with abalone liver, a restorative breakfast tied to the island's haenyeo diving women.

places.name: Myeongjin Jeonbok
places.note: Island institution for abalone porridge and abalone stone-pot rice.

places.name: Haenyeoui Jip
places.note: Run by the diving women's cooperative; whatever they landed that morning.

places.name: Dongmun Traditional Market
places.note: Several stalls do a cheap, quick bowl without the drive out of town.

food.name: Gogi-guksu pork noodles
food.desc: Fat wheat noodles in a milky pork-bone broth topped with sliced belly, the everyday Jeju bowl eaten at weddings and hangovers alike.

places.name: Olle Guksu
places.note: The best-known noodle house in Jeju City; go early to skip the line.

places.name: Gogi-guksu Street
places.note: A whole lane of noodle shops competing on the same dish.

food.name: Galchi hairtail
food.desc: Silvery hairtail from Jeju waters, either braised with radish and chilli or salt-grilled whole and eaten with rice.

places.name: Dongmun Traditional Market
places.note: Buy it at the fish stalls or eat it cooked at the market restaurants.

places.name: Yongdam-dong seafood houses
places.note: Coastal restaurants specialising in braised and grilled hairtail sets.

food.name: Omegi-tteok
food.desc: Chewy millet or buckwheat rice cakes rolled in red bean, a Jeju highland sweet sold warm at the island's markets.

places.name: Dongmun Traditional Market
places.note: Stalls sell it fresh by the piece alongside other island snacks.

places.name: Jeju Folk Five-Day Market
places.note: Huge periodic market; best for homemade versions and omegi liquor.

food.name: Hallabong citrus juice
food.desc: Jeju's bumpy sweet hallabong oranges are pressed fresh, blended into ade or dried into tea; a citrus grown almost nowhere else.

places.name: Dongmun Traditional Market
places.note: Juice stands press hallabong to order; also sells peel tea and jam.

places.name: Tapdong seaside cafes
places.note: Waterfront cafes serve hallabong ade and citrus desserts.

food.name: Jeju wit ale and omegi-sul
food.desc: A tangerine-peel wheat beer brewed on the island, plus omegi-sul, the traditional Jeju millet liquor.

places.name: Jeju Beer brewery
places.note: Working brewery with tours and a taproom pouring the wit ale fresh.

places.name: Tapdong bars
places.note: Seafront bars stock island beers and traditional Jeju spirits.

places.name: Dongmun Traditional Market
places.note: Good place to pick up bottled omegi-sul to take home.

landmarks: Hallasan National Park
South Korea's highest peak, a shield volcano crowned by a crater lake, whose trails climb through fields of spring azaleas above Jeju City.
Manjanggul Lava Tube
A UNESCO-listed lava tunnel stretching for kilometres beneath the island, culminating in the world's tallest known lava column.
Yongduam Rock (Dragon Head Rock)
A wave-battered volcanic outcrop shaped like a roaring dragon, Jeju City's signature coastal photo spot, dramatic at sunset.
Dongmun Traditional Market
Jeju's liveliest market since 1945, stacked with hallabong oranges, black-pork skewers and fresh seafood in a maze of covered arcades.
Samseonghyeol Shrine
A wooded sanctuary sheltering the three holes from which Jeju's legendary founding demigods are said to have emerged.
Iho Tewoo Beach
The city's nearest beach, famous for its pair of horse-shaped lighthouses in red and white guarding the harbor entrance.
Yongyeon Pond and Cloud Bridge
A serene cliff-lined pond where freshwater meets the sea, spanned by a pavilion bridge that glows colorfully after dark.
Hamdeok Beach
A postcard bay of white sand and gin-clear turquoise water east of the city, backed by the gentle Seoubong volcanic hill.
Jeju Folk and Natural History Museum
An engaging introduction to the island's volcanic geology and the traditions of its haenyeo free-diving women.
Gwandeokjeong Pavilion
Jeju Island's oldest surviving building, a 1448 Joseon-era pavilion in the city centre painted with murals of longevity symbols and famed battle scenes.

train.note: Jeju has no railway anywhere on the island; getting around means buses, rental cars or taxis.

bus.note: No overland connections exist — Jeju is an island. On the island, an extensive colour-coded intercity and city bus network (overhauled in the 2017 reform, with free transfers) covers everywhere from the Jeju Bus Terminal; pay with a T-money card.

ferry.note: Jeju's ferries are domestic links to the Korean mainland: Hanil Express car ferries sail from Jeju to Wando (about 2h45), and Seaworld Express ferries run to Mokpo (about 4h30); longer sailings connect Jeju with Busan. All leave from Jeju Port — book via the operators or the Korean ferry portal (https://island.haewoon.co.kr).

half.name: Manjanggul Cave
half.blurb: One of the world's finest lava tubes, a UNESCO site with a giant lava column, on the northeast coast.

half.name: Hyeopjae Beach & Hallim Park
half.blurb: A white-sand beach with turquoise water beside subtropical gardens and lava caves on the west coast.

full.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
full.blurb: The 'Sunrise Peak', a dramatic UNESCO tuff crater rising from the sea on the east coast, about an hour away.

full.name: Seogwipo & waterfalls
full.blurb: Jeju's southern city, home to the Cheonjiyeon and Jeongbang waterfalls and the Olle coastal walking trails.

full.name: Udo Island
full.blurb: A tiny island off the east coast, toured by bike or scooter for its beaches and haenyeo divers.
